15710.q: Which historic capital is famous for Gyeongbokgung Palace and was built at the start of the Joseon Dynasty?
15710.e: Hanyang (한양) was the capital founded by the Joseon Dynasty in 1394. It became modern Seoul. Gyeongbokgung was the main royal palace built there.

15708.q: What event destroyed the original Tripitaka Koreana in the 13th century?
15708.e: The Mongol invasions of the 13th century destroyed the original. Koreans remade the work on more than 80,000 wooden blocks, which are still preserved at Haeinsa.

15707.q: What is the name of the 1980 pro-democracy movement that ended in a brutal massacre under South Korea's military dictatorship?
15707.e: The Gwangju Uprising (광주 민주화 운동) of May 1980 was a pro-democracy movement brutally suppressed under General Chun Doo-hwan, resulting in hundreds of deaths.

15706.q: Which printing technology was developed in Korea before Gutenberg, during the Goryeo period?
15706.e: Korea developed metal movable type around 1230 CE, more than 200 years before Gutenberg in Europe. The "Jikji" (1377) is the oldest surviving book printed with metal movable type.

15705.q: What was the name of the Korean kingdom in the Middle Ages that gave rise to the name "Korea" in Western languages?
15705.e: The Goryeo dynasty (고려, 918–1392) gave rise to the name "Korea": Arab and Persian merchants traded with that kingdom and carried the name to the West.

15704.q: Which Korean empress was assassinated by Japanese agents in 1895?
15704.e: Empress Myeongseong (명성황후), also known as "Queen Min", was assassinated by Japanese agents at Gyeongbok Palace in October 1895.

15702.q: In what year did South Korea co-host the FIFA World Cup, reaching the semifinals?
15702.e: The 2002 World Cup was co-hosted by South Korea and Japan. South Korea surprised the world by reaching the semifinals, the best result ever by an Asian national team.

15701.q: Which Korean admiral is legendary for defeating the Japanese naval invasion in the 16th century with "turtle ships"?
15701.e: Admiral Yi Sun-sin (이순신) is Korea's most revered military hero, famous for using the geobukseon (turtle ships) to defend the country during the Japanese invasions of 1592–1598.

15700.q: What is the name of the Korean state legendarily founded by Dangun more than 4,000 years ago?
15700.e: Gojoseon (고조선, "Old Joseon") is the first Korean state, legendarily founded by Dangun in 2333 BCE, and is the root of Korean national identity.

15699.q: Which three kingdoms made up the period that preceded Korean unification?
15699.e: The Three Kingdoms period (삼국 시대) consists of Goguryeo (north), Baekje (southwest) and Silla (southeast), which existed from roughly 57 BCE to 668 CE.

15698.q: Which city hosted the 1988 Summer Olympics?
15698.e: Seoul hosted the 1988 Summer Olympics, a milestone for South Korea that showed the country's modernization to the world.

15697.q: Who was the first president of the Republic of Korea (South Korea)?
15697.e: Syngman Rhee (이승만) was the first president of the Republic of Korea, serving from 1948 to 1960, when he resigned after the April Revolution protests.

15696.q: What is the name of the Korean independence movement against Japanese occupation that began on March 1, 1919?
15696.e: The March 1st Movement (삼일운동, Sam-il Undong) of 1919 was one of the first public demonstrations of resistance to Japanese occupation, with thousands of Koreans taking to the streets to demand independence.

15695.q: What was the "Miracle on the Han River"?
o: South Korea's rapid industrialization and economic growth
15695.e: The "Miracle on the Han River" (한강의 기적) refers to South Korea's extraordinary economic growth after the Korean War, going from one of the poorest countries to one of the largest economies in just decades.

15694.q: Which power colonized Korea from 1910 to 1945?
15694.e: Japan colonized Korea from 1910 to 1945, a period of severe cultural suppression and economic exploitation that ended with Japan's defeat in World War II.

15693.q: When did the Korean War begin?
15693.e: The Korean War began on June 25, 1950, when North Korea invaded South Korea. The conflict lasted until the armistice of July 1953.

15692.q: In what year was Korea divided into North and South?
15692.e: The division of Korea took place in 1945, after the end of World War II, along the 38th parallel north. The North came under Soviet influence and the South under American influence.

15691.q: Which Korean king is considered one of history's greatest monarchs for creating Hangul?
15691.e: King Sejong the Great (세종대왕, r. 1418–1450) is considered Korea's greatest monarch, responsible for creating Hangul and for major scientific and cultural advances.

15690.q: Which dynasty ruled Korea for more than 500 years, until 1897?
15690.e: The Joseon Dynasty (조선) ruled Korea from 1392 to 1897.

15862.q: Which president is famous for the "Miracle on the Han River", Korea's economic growth?
15862.e: Park Chung-hee (1961–1979) led South Korea's rapid economic growth, the "Miracle on the Han River".

15860.q: Which kingdom unified the Korean peninsula for the first time?
15860.e: The Kingdom of Silla unified Korea in 668 CE, establishing the Unified Silla period.

15866.q: In what year did South Korea formally become a democracy?
15866.e: In 1987 the Constitution was revised to guarantee direct elections, marking the democratic transition.

15875.q: In what year did a Korean win the Nobel Peace Prize?
15875.e: Kim Dae-jung received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2000 for his efforts toward reconciliation with North Korea.

15885.q: What was the 2016–2017 "Candlelight Movement" in South Korea?
o: Protests that led to the impeachment of President Park Geun-hye
15885.e: The Candlelight Movement brought millions to the streets demanding the impeachment of Park Geun-hye, which was carried out in 2017.

15882.q: What was the outcome of the Cairo Conference (1943) regarding Korea?
o: It declared that Korea would be independent after the war
It divided Korea into zones of influence
It handed Korea to American control
15882.e: The Cairo Declaration (1943) promised that Korea would be free and independent "in due course" after Japan's defeat.

15872.q: What was the main cause of the Japanese invasion of Korea in 1592?
o: Toyotomi Hideyoshi was trying to conquer China by passing through Korea
15872.e: Toyotomi Hideyoshi invaded Korea in 1592 (the Imjin War), using it as a route to conquer China.

15874.q: What was the role of the "chaebols" in Korea's economic development?
o: Large family-run conglomerates that led industrialization
15874.e: Chaebols such as Samsung, Hyundai and LG were fundamental to South Korea's rapid industrialization.

15881.q: What was the Gabo Reform movement (1894–1896)?
o: A series of modernizing reforms that abolished Korea's caste system
15881.e: The Gabo Reforms abolished slavery and the caste system and modernized several Korean institutions.

32815.q: In what year did Yuna Kim become Olympic champion in figure skating?
32815.e: Yuna Kim won Olympic gold in women's singles figure skating in 2010.

32819.q: Yuna Kim won the Grand Prix Final in figure skating three times. In which seasons?
32819.e: Yuna Kim won the Grand Prix Final in the 2006–2007, 2007–2008 and 2009–2010 seasons.

32817.q: In how many editions was Yuna Kim world champion in figure skating?
32817.e: Yuna Kim was world champion in 2009 and 2013.

32816.q: At which Olympics did Yuna Kim win the silver medal?
32816.e: Yuna Kim won silver at the Sochi Olympics in 2014.

15858.q: What are the "Haenyeo" in Korean culture?
o: Traditional women divers from Jeju Island
15858.e: The Haenyeo are women divers from Jeju Island, inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

15853.q: In what year was Hangul (the Korean writing system) created?
15853.e: Hangul was created in 1443 by King Sejong of the Joseon dynasty to increase literacy among the people.

o: A traditional music genre with dramatic storytelling
15852.e: Pansori is a traditional Korean music genre recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

o: A deep feeling of melancholy and collective resilience
15612.e: "Han" is a Korean cultural concept that describes a complex emotion of sorrow, resentment and hope, very present in Korean arts and history.

15848.q: What was the role of the Saemaul Undong movement in 1970s Korea?
o: Modernization and development of rural villages
15848.e: Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) was a movement by the Park Chung-hee government to modernize rural areas.

o: A deep emotional bond that forms over time
15847.e: "Jeong" is a uniquely Korean concept that describes a deep emotional bond built through time spent together.

15687.q: What is the name of the Seoul neighborhood famous for its fashion trends and nightlife?
15687.e: Hongdae (홍대) is the neighborhood near Hongik University, famous for its art scene, live music, alternative fashion and nightlife.

o: Affectionate physical contact between close friends
15845.e: "Skinship" refers to non-romantic physical contact between friends, such as holding hands or hugging.

o: A video of someone eating large amounts of food
15844.e: Mukbang (먹방) is a Korean phenomenon of live streams in which people eat large amounts of food.

15843.q: What is the importance of Seollal (Lunar New Year) in Korea?
o: It is the most important holiday, when families gather
It is just a commercial holiday
It celebrates the start of summer
It is a festival only for young people
15843.e: Seollal is the Korean Lunar New Year, when families gather to perform sebae (formal bows) and eat a festive meal.

15842.e: Dduk (떡), usually romanized as tteok, are Korea's famous rice cakes, used in many preparations such as tteokbokki.

15675.q: What does the "finger heart" gesture, popular in Korean culture, mean?
15675.e: The "finger heart" is a popular gesture in Korea that represents love or affection, widely used by K-pop idols.

o: A culture of hurry and efficiency
15840.e: "Bbali-bbali" (빨리빨리) represents the Korean culture of doing everything quickly and with urgency.

15836.q: What is a "PC bang" in South Korea?
o: A Korean internet cafe for gaming
15836.e: PC bangs (PC방) are Korean internet cafes, popular places to play online games.

15835.q: What is the purpose of "noraebang" in Korea?
15835.e: Noraebang (노래방) are private karaoke rooms where groups of friends sing together.

15834.e: "Jesa" is a Korean ritual to honor ancestors, held on commemorative dates.

15833.q: Which Confucian value still influences modern Korean society?
15833.e: Confucianism still deeply influences Korea, especially in respect for age and hierarchy.

15832.q: What does the "10-step skincare" mean in the context of K-beauty?
o: A Korean skin care routine with 10 steps
15832.e: The 10-step routine is a Korean skin care practice that includes double cleansing, essences and more.

15831.q: What is the concept of "nunchi" in Korean culture?
o: The ability to read the room and react appropriately
15831.e: "Nunchi" (눈치) is the social skill of picking up subtle cues in the environment, highly valued in Korea.

15830.q: What is the name of Seoul's most famous palace?
15830.e: Gyeongbokgung is the largest and most famous of Seoul's five grand palaces, built in 1395.

o: A Korean digital comic published online
15829.e: Webtoons are manhwa published in a digital, vertical format adapted for smartphones.

15828.q: What is the most popular alcoholic drink in Korea?
15828.e: Soju is a distilled drink with an alcohol content of between 16% and 25%, and one of the best-selling spirits in the world.

15827.e: Manhwa (만화) are Korean comics, the equivalent of Japanese manga.

15826.q: How do you say "thank you" in Korean?
15826.e: "Gamsahamnida" (감사합니다) is the formal way to say "thank you" in Korean.

15825.q: What is the main ingredient of bibimbap?
15825.e: Bibimbap (비빔밥) is rice mixed with vegetables, meat, egg and chili paste (gochujang).

o: The Korean beauty and cosmetics industry
15824.e: K-beauty (Korean beauty) refers to South Korea's cosmetics industry and beauty trends.

15823.e: "Oppa" (오빠) is used by women to refer to an older man they are close to.

15822.q: What is the capital of South Korea?
15822.e: Seoul is South Korea's capital and largest city, with around 10 million people.

15821.e: Hanbok (한복) is traditional Korean clothing, with centuries of history.

o: A Korean harvest festival, similar to Thanksgiving
15820.e: Chuseok is one of the biggest Korean holidays, celebrated on the 15th day of the 8th lunar month to give thanks for the harvest.

15819.q: What is the name of the Korean lantern festival held for Buddha's birthday?
15819.e: Yeon Deung Hoe is the Lantern Festival, held to honor the birth of Buddha.

15817.q: What is aegyo in K-pop culture?
15817.e: Aegyo (애교) is the art of acting cute and charming, highly valued in Korean pop culture.

15816.q: What is South Korea's national dish?
15816.e: Kimchi, made of fermented vegetables (usually cabbage), is Korea's most iconic dish.

o: The Korean Wave: the spread of Korean culture around the world
The name of a K-pop group
15815.e: Hallyu (한류) means "Korean Wave" and refers to the global spread of South Korea's pop culture.

15685.q: What is the name of the Korean writing system, created in the 15th century?
15685.e: Hangul (한글) was created by King Sejong the Great and his scholars in 1443, during the Joseon Dynasty, to increase literacy among the Korean people.

15682.q: Which Korean film won the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival in 2019?
15682.e: "Parasite" (기생충), by director Bong Joon-ho, won the Palme d'Or at Cannes 2019 and later the Oscar for Best Picture in 2020.

15681.q: What is the name of the Korean bronze percussion instrument similar to a gong?
15681.e: The kkwaenggwari (꽹과리) is a small bronze gong used in Korean folk music, especially nongak (farmers' music).

15680.q: What is the name of the Korean ritual of paying respects to ancestors during Chuseok and Seollal?
15680.e: Charye (차례) is the ancestral offering ritual held during Seollal and Chuseok, when the family prepares special foods and performs formal bows.

15678.q: What is the name of the Korean martial art that became an Olympic sport?
15678.e: Taekwondo is the Korean martial art that became an official Olympic sport at the Sydney 2000 Games. It is known for its acrobatic kicks.

15673.q: What is the name of the Korean festival that celebrates the Lunar New Year?
15673.e: Seollal (설날) is the Korean Lunar New Year, one of the country's most important holidays, when families gather to honor ancestors and share meals.

15613.q: What does "comeback" mean in the context of K-pop?
o: A new album or single release by an already active artist
15613.e: In K-pop, "comeback" is used for any new release by an active artist, not necessarily a return after an absence.

o: The top prize at music award ceremonies
15609.e: "Daesang" (대상) means "Grand Prize". It is the top award at ceremonies such as MAMA and the Golden Disc Awards.

15607.q: What is the name of the illegal practice of buying albums in bulk to manipulate the charts?
15607.e: "Sajaegi" (사재기) is the illegal bulk purchase of albums or streams. It has caused several scandals in K-pop.

15605.q: What is the trainee system in K-pop?
15605.e: Trainees spend years training in singing, dancing and languages at agencies before debuting as idols.

15602.e: "Daebak" (대박) means something amazing or great luck. It is used a lot in K-dramas and by fandoms.

35055.q: What does the name Fin.K.L stand for?

35054.q: Fin.K.L is considered a historic rival of which group?
35054.e: Fin.K.L and S.E.S. were the main rival girl groups of the 1990s.

35053.q: In what year did Fin.K.L debut?

35052.e: Fin.K.L was formed by DSP Media.

35050.q: In what year did S.E.S. debut?

35049.q: Where does the name S.E.S. come from?
o: The initials of members Sea, Eugene and Shoo
An English acronym with no connection
35049.e: S.E.S. comes from the initials of Sea, Eugene and Shoo.

35048.e: S.E.S. was launched by SM Entertainment in 1997.
